+# Postmortem: Edge Client Request Jitter & Booklogr API Latency
+
+## Root Cause
+The `booklogr-api` service was configured to fetch external book metadata from `openlibrary` (`https://openlibrary.org/search.json`) and fallback to `https://metadata.booklogr.app`. In this environment, external internet endpoints are unreachable and time out after 30 seconds per request. Because `BookProvider` attempted external HTTP requests with long timeouts before falling back, Gunicorn worker threads became saturated and blocked for up to 30–60 seconds per search request. This caused elevated p99 latency (`BooklogrApiLatencyP99High`) and request jitter on the edge client (`EdgeClientRequestJitter`). Meanwhile, the local metadata container (`http://book-metadata:8080`) was available but idle (`BookMetadataTrafficStalled`).
+
+## Evidence Used
+- Alertmanager alerts (`EdgeClientRequestJitter`, `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High`) and Prometheus rules (`BookMetadataTrafficStalled`).
+- Prometheus metrics showing `/v1/books/search` average duration exceeding 1.3–2.5s and `book-metadata:8080` target metrics.
+- `curl` timeouts when attempting connections to `openlibrary.org` (error 28) versus sub-10ms response from `http://book-metadata:8080/v1/search/<query>`.
+- Source code in `api/config.py` and `api/book_provider.py` showing default data providers set to `openlibrary` and `https://metadata.booklogr.app`.
+
+## Changes Made
+- Updated `DATA_PROVIDER` and `DATA_PROVIDER_FALLBACK` in `api/config.py` to use the local metadata service (`http://book-metadata:8080`).
+- Modified `api/book_provider.py` to route external provider defaults (`openlibrary` and `https://metadata.booklogr.app`) to `http://book-metadata:8080`, added circuit-breaker fast failover, and reduced HTTP request timeouts.
